Today's big story
BTC clears $80K as Visa-Bridge stablecoin rails go live in 18 countries.
Bitcoin printed an $80,058 handle overnight — first close above the level this leg — on the same day Visa and Bridge confirmed stablecoin-linked cards are live in 18 countries with 100 by year-end. OKX Singapore lit up its USDC/USDT/USDG Visa card last month. MoonPay launched a stablecoin debit card for AI agents on Mastercard. Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said stablecoin economics "look just like our normal product." The pipes for tokenized money are being laid before the next macro leg.

ORDI ran +37.9% to $6.05 on $80K BTC, dragging the Bitcoin Ordinals basket back into focus after a quiet stretch. When BTC clears a round number, the on-chain BTC-native plays move first — ORDI is the highest-beta proxy. Illustrative only, not advice.
01 — Fintech pulse
Stablecoin cards go global — the rails are being laid in plain sight.
Visa CEO Ryan McInerney told investors stablecoin economics "look just like our normal product" while disclosing a $4.6B annualized stablecoin-settlement run rate. Bridge-issued, Visa-branded stablecoin cards are now live in 18 countries with a target of 100 by year-end. OKX Singapore launched a USDC/USDT/USDG-funded Visa card last month. MoonPay shipped MoonAgents Card on Mastercard for AI agents to spend onchain balances at the merchant tier. The settlement layer the cycle was waiting for is shipping.
Stablecoin transaction volume is on a glide path to overtake combined Visa + Mastercard flows this decade — not because consumers care about the chain, but because the float, the rebates, and the FX spread now route through code instead of correspondent banks. With BTC clearing $80K, NQ at all-time highs, and the May FOMC pricing a hold, the macro is the side dish; the structural shift to onchain money is the main course.
TRADE ON SWOP →
02 — Swop spotlight
When the card is a wallet, the wallet has to be Swop.
Visa-Bridge stablecoin cards going live in 100 countries is the death knell for the "ramp on, ramp off" CEX model. The card swipes the wallet directly — whatever USDC, USDT, or USDG is sitting onchain spends at the point of sale. The asset never leaves self-custody. The exchange middleman gets disintermediated. The wallet is the bank.
Swop is built for exactly this moment. Crypto Spot for the BTC and ETH bag. Swop Perps for the leveraged macro view on the FOMC and jobs report. Swop Predictions for the playoff series and PMI prints. Tokenized Stocks for SPY, QQQ, and the AI basket — all settling into the same self-custody wallet on Polygon, Base, Ethereum, or Solana. One key. One balance. Four trade surfaces.
When stablecoins are the rail and the wallet is the bank, the winner is whoever owns the surface. That's Swop.
EXPLORE SWOP →
03 — Day ahead
What to watch — macro, courts, and tonight's board.
📅 Macro Calendar
• 8:30 ET (May 5) — March Trade Balance — tariff pass-through watch
• 9:45 ET (May 5) — S&P Final Services PMI (April) — cross-check vs ISM
• 10:00 ET (May 5) — ISM Services PMI (April) — biggest print of the week before payrolls
• 8:30 ET (May 8) — April Employment Situation (payrolls + unemployment) — the print that prices the June FOMC
⚖ Court Watch
• Clarity Act — Senate market-structure bill back on the floor calendar; stablecoin yield carve-out is the live debate
• GENIUS Act implementation — Treasury rules on 1:1 reserves and monthly attestations rolling out; first issuer attestations due this quarter
• State-level pressure — NYDFS and CA DFPI are now the active regulators; SEC has dropped crypto from its 2026 priorities entirely
🎯 Tonight's Games · Swop Predictions vs. the Books
• Lakers @ Thunder (NBA West Semis G1 · 8:30 ET, NBC/Peacock) — OKC defending champs at home; Swop Predictions series line richer on LAL than books
• Wild @ Avalanche (NHL West 2nd Round G2 · 8 ET, ESPN) — COL home favorite; series 1-0 COL; totals-side divergence vs books
• MLB Tuesday slate — full 15-game board, divisional matchups headlined by Yankees/Dodgers tilts — Swop Predictions surfaces moneyline + totals across the slate
